reports.text: Lake Cachuma Fishing Guide Report 10/14/2026 - This is one of our clients that came out with this week to do some bass fishing at beautiful Lake Cachuma, fishing the fall bite catching a plenty of bass on a variety of baits, as can be seen in the pictures below.

reports.title: Lake Cachuma Fishing Guide Report
reports.text: Lake Cachuma Fishing Guide Report 10/07/2026 - Here’s a few trips that I had, yesterday and today at beautiful Lake Cachuma, Santa Barbara, ca, catching some really nice bass on a variety of baits.

reports.title: Anglers reported another good week of bass fishing
reports.text: The lake remained near 35 percent of its storage capacity, and anglers reported another good week of bass fishing. The crappie bite remained strong around submerged stumps in about 15 feet of water, where small swimbaits and minijigs produced fish.

reports.title: Fishing was decent at Hart Park
reports.text: Fishing was decent at Hart Park, with anglers reporting good numbers of smaller bass. Anglers also punched plastics through the heavier grass, and a few better-quality bass fell for medium sized paddle tail swimbaits.

reports.title: Anglers reported decent fall fishing at Buena Vista Lakes
reports.text: Bass anglers found largemouth along submerged weed lines, near the islands, and around submerged brush. Crappie were found around submerged rocks and brush, where small live minnows, minijigs, and small swimbaits produced bites.

reports.title: The bass bite at Lake Ming remains fair
reports.text: The bass bite at Lake Ming remains fair, with anglers finding success on shaky heads, micro jigs, and small Senkos. Downsizing presentations has been the key to generating more bites. Catfish continue to stay active and are being caught on anchovies, sardines, and dip bait. There have been no recent reports of carp, while bluegill are biting well on live worms.

reports.title: At River Walk, bass activity has been improving
reports.text: At River Walk, bass activity has been improving, with the best action coming during the early morning and late evening hours.

reports.title: Lake Isabella has dropped slightly to 25 percent of capacity, but the bass bite remains solid
reports.text: Lake Isabella has dropped slightly to 25 percent of capacity, but the bass bite remains solid, with water temperatures holding around 75 degrees. As the day progresses, Texas-rigged 8- to 10-inch Rusty’s Big Worms in purple and black/blue have been producing quality bass around brush piles and points in 5 to 20 feet of water. The crappie bite improved this week, with several reports of quality stringers coming in.
